name: The Populus nigra of via Don Lorenzo Milani
reason: New find, 2026-08-31 pass, not previously recorded. 6.7 km from centre, girth 5.4 m despite an age band under 100 years, so a fast-growing giant rather than an ancient tree; potentially visually spectacular on size alone. Reverse-geocodes to via Don Lorenzo Milani, Ricovero, Collegno, a separate comune west of Torino, not the city itself. One targeted search ("pioppo nero monumentale Collegno") found the Comune di Collegno's own municipal tree census page exists but returned no specific hit for this tree, and no press coverage. No second source, no place name, no confirmed park/access context, and it would need its own day-trip justification (transit time from Torino centre) rather than joining this walk. Worth a look next pass with a direct fetch of Collegno's tree census, not chased further this pass.

name: The wide plane east of the Po
reason: Second widest trunk in the city at 6.4 m and yet only 14 m tall, which almost certainly means a pollarded or topped tree. Neither the tourist route nor either press list names it, so it has no place name at all yet and no second source. Worth a look because of the girth, but the height ratio needs explaining before it could be written. CHECKED 2026-08-23: this is NOT the press-documented 'plane of Corso Novara by the Cimitero Monumentale' (see that separate, already-blocked lead below); this point sits about 1.8km further southeast, on the Sassi hillside. A reverse geocode of the coordinate returns 'Villa Rey' as the nearest named OSM feature, roughly 250m off, which may just be sparse tagging on that hillside rather than evidence the tree stands on Villa Rey's own grounds (Villa Rey's registered plane, reg_id 009, is a separate point 1.8km away and is itself blocked on access, see above). Still no name, no second source and no confirmed access status. Do not ship without a real site identification; worth a look at Google Street View or a Sassi/Madonna del Pilone neighbourhood association page next pass. CHECKED AGAIN 2026-08-31: Nominatim reverse geocode places the exact point at 92 int. 119, Corso Quintino Sella, Madonna del Pilone, within Torino proper (Circoscrizione 7, Sassi). Three separate searches this pass (platano + Madonna del Pilone/Sassi/Corso Quintino Sella; platano + Sassi/collina Po/censimento; platano + Villa Rey/Borgata Sassi) and one attempted fetch of the torinocronaca.it 16-monumental-trees survey and the 5wagora.com monumental-trees article (both loaded fine and list all 16 named register trees by park) found this tree in neither: it genuinely has no press coverage and no place name anywhere found, confirming the 2026-08-23 finding rather than overturning it. Register remains the sole source. Still a lead, not shippable without a second source under BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's two-source bar.

name: The Weeping Ash at Palac Puslowskich (ul. Pulawska 97)
species: European Ash, weeping form (Fraxinus excelsior f. pendula)
reason: A distinctive weeping-form ash, register-described as a remnant of a former palace park, standing around Palac Puslowskich (built 1862 for Ksawery Puslowski, designed by Henryk Marconi; historically the Instytut Moralnej Poprawy Dzieci, a childrens reform institute, per warszawyhistoriaukryta.blogspot.com and blogi.kukushka.eu). Current occupant/use and whether the grounds are open to walk-in visitors were NOT established this pass (ran out of budget after the palace-history search); a fotopolska.eu link that looked promising turned out to describe a different ash tree entirely (ul. Pustola, Wola) and was discarded per the search-summary-is-a-lead rule. 0.64km from war_009 and 0.46km from war_005, would fit the cluster well if access clears. Needs: current occupant of the palace/grounds and whether the tree stands on a public pavement or inside the institutional grounds. UPDATE 2026-08-31: established the current occupant, which the previous pass could not: Mlodziezowy Dom Kultury (MDK Mokotow), a youth culture centre, has occupied the palace since 1 January 1968 (whu.org.pl) and still operates there today (mdk-mokotow.pl). It publishes visiting/office hours (secretariat Mon-Thu 9-17, described elsewhere as open Mon-Thu 8-20 and Sat 8-14, closed Fri/Sun) and a playground/small garden area at Pulawska 97B is mentioned by a directory listing, which suggests routine walk-in use rather than an appointment-only site. But no source describes the grounds, a garden or the tree itself, or states plainly that a member of the public (not enrolled in a class) may walk onto the property to see it, so this does not yet clear the honest access-line test. Leaving as a lead rather than shipping or blocking; a session that can browse mdk-mokotow.pl's photo galleries or Google Street View/Maps reviews, or a reader visit, would likely settle it quickly.

name: Wallace Yew
species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
why: Verified and NOT shipped, 2026-08-29. Alive as of a 2021 photograph and behind a protective fence at Elderslie beside the Wallace monument, but wrecked: set on fire in 1978, and a storm on 12 January 2005 tore away the better-growing half and split the trunk almost to the ground. Age is genuinely disputed rather than merely unknown, 300 years by expert estimate against a 700-year tradition tying it to William Wallace himself, with 18th-century parish records already calling it ancient. Source: scotlands-yew-trees.org. Held on the walk-across-town test rather than on any rule; revisit if a recent photograph shows it worth the trip.

name: Aguaribay del Perito Moreno
why: Excellent facts otherwise: planted in 1872 by explorer Francisco 'Perito' Moreno on his own estate (per his own unpublished memoirs, verified by Argentina's National Commission of Monuments), the school later built on the site (Instituto Bernasconi, Catulo Castillo 2750, Parque Patricios) was moved 10 metres during construction specifically to avoid removing the tree, and it was Argentina's first tree declared a national historic monument (Decreto Nacional 3.369/1943 per Argentina.gob.ar; press sources also cite Decreto 2.232/1943, likely a mix-up with the later 1946 magnolia/pacara decree, worth resolving before publishing). BLOCKED FROM SHIPPING THIS PASS on access only: sources agree the tree stands within the Instituto's own grounds/interior park ('dentro del predio, no sobre la vereda'), which is a functioning public school of over 3,600 students. The complex does house two public museums people visit (Geografico 'Juan B. Teran' and Ciencias Naturales 'Angel Gallardo'), which suggests some real public access exists, but no source found this pass confirmed whether the tree itself sits in a part of the grounds reachable during those visits, or whether it is visible from Catulo Castillo street over a fence/gate. A follow-up pass should check for a street-view/photo showing the tree from outside the grounds, or a museum-visit description that places it on the visitable route, before this ships as either a full entry or a view-only one.

name: The Nolina of the Orto Botanico
why: 560 cm at the base and 4 m tall, the second widest registered trunk in the whole garden and visually the strangest thing in it, a huge swollen succulent foot. Held back on one point only, and it is the species. MASAF calls it Nolina longifolia, Campania scheda 163 calls it Nolina recurvata, and those are two different plants, not two names for one. Both are now placed in Beaucarnea and both are Italian 'pianta mangiafumo', so the common name cannot break the tie either. The garden's own desert and arboretum pages do not list it at all, so there is no third opinion online. Everything else verifies: both registers give the same 560 cm at the same point. Publishing genus-only was considered and rejected, since no entry in the corpus does that and hard rule 9 keys the species pages on the binomial. To resolve: read the plant label on site, or ask the garden. Then it ships.

name: Dab Nestor
why: Researched this pass. Two independent sources agree closely on facts: the GDOS register (designated 2009-02-17, PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.0264011.2380) and a dedicated page on drzeworoku.pl (a Polish tree-of-the-year competition site), which gives species Quercus robur, age ~220 years, height ~20m, girth 435cm, and history (planted 19th century, preserved through postwar redevelopment, later adopted and named by Primary School No. 50, ul. It stands on public land between the Manuel Gimenez Abad bridge of the Tercer Cinturon and the railway bridge, which is exactly the problem: it is a road-and-rail margin rather than a place anyone walks to, roughly 900 m southeast of Parque Bruil with no pleasant route between. The book already noted it was short of water because the irrigation channel beside it had been altered. Keep as the candidate if the Huerva riverside path is ever made continuous.

name: The Field Elms of Camino de Enmedio, La Cartuja
why: Two registered field elms on the same lane in La Cartuja Baja, 2.50 m and 2.20 m round, both 'bueno' in 2005, with a registered white mulberry a short way along the same camino. Mature field elms are worth attention anywhere because Dutch elm disease removed most of them, and three registered trees on one rural lane is a genuine small cluster. La Cartuja Baja is 8 km southeast of the centre and inside the day-trip boundary by city bus. Needs a survival check, since elms are exactly the species that quietly go, and the book already flagged that the lane had recently been concreted over one of them. CHECKED 2026-08-15: a Wikiloc trail description of this exact stretch (Pabellon Principe Felipe to La Cartuja Baja via Camino de Enmedio) still lists 'arboles singulares de moral y olmo' along the path, which is real but general corroboration that at least one elm and the mulberry survive; it does not say which of the two registered elms, so the concreted-over one still cannot be identified. Not written: the register already flagged one specimen as directly threatened and a general trail blurb cannot rule out that it was the one lost. Next step: streetlevel imagery or a more specific, dated source.
